summary: Seven iterations have validated a hierarchical 'bracket' search algorithm for BLIS configuration optimization across H100 and A100 hardware, confirming that TP=4/2-instance dominates hard workloads and that Bayesian (TPE) search finds the optimum ~2x faster than random. The current frontier is generalization: L40S hardware (first tested in iter-2) shows a tighter TP margin (2.1% vs 8.3% on H100) and model-dependent TP winners — the bracket algorithm is predicted to handle this but has not been run end-to-end on L40S yet. The next iteration will confirm L40S generalization and BLIS seed robustness (seeds 42–46) as independent axes.
key_points: CONFIRMED (iter-1, h-main): TPE finds the global best ~2x faster than random search (evals_to_best 18.8 vs 36.2 at budget=50) and advantage grows under high load (6.87% fitness gap at rate=200 vs 5.36% at rate=50); LHS matches TPE at budget=50, suggesting the fitness landscape is structured enough for stratified sampling.

CONFIRMED (iter-1, h-robustness): TP=8/1-instance dominates easy/low-request regimes; TP=4/2-instance dominates hard/high-request regimes on H100 and A100 — this ranking is stable across 5 BLIS seeds on H100 (7–10% margin) but narrows to 0.86–3.4% on L40S, raising the question of whether bracket Phase 1 reliably picks the correct winner in tight-margin cases.

STILL UNKNOWN (next iteration focus): (1) Whether bracket K=1 correctly selects TP=4 on L40S hard llama end-to-end across all 5 search seeds, given the 2.1% margin (vs 8.3% on H100); (2) whether workload seed variation (blis_seeds 42–46) flips the TP ranking on L40S at the tightest observed margin (seed 44: 0.86% gap); (3) whether qwen3-14b on L40S (where TP=8 wins, uniquely) is handled correctly by the bracket algorithm — reserved for iter-3.

UNEXPECTED: The TP winner on L40S is model-dependent (llama-3.1-8b → TP=4/2inst; qwen3-14b → TP=8/1inst), a regime not seen on H100/A100, attributed to L40S's low bandwidth (0.864 TB/s) interacting differently with 8B vs 14B parameter weight-loading overhead.

REFUTED (iter-1, h-control-negative): The prediction that TPE has no advantage over random in a 15-point search space was wrong — TPE was 2.2x faster even there, because TP=8's 13% score advantage creates a strongly unimodal landscape that TPE's surrogate model exploits regardless of space size.
